title: Short Stuff: Flappers
summary: Short Stuff episode on flappers, the 1920s young women who rejected Victorian norms. Covers H. L. Mencken's 1915 essay introducing the term in The Smart Set, the Gibson Girl look they replaced, the impact of World War I and the 1918 flu on women's roles, the 18th and 19th Amendments (Prohibition and women's suffrage), the rise of automobiles and radio (KDKA), flapper fashion (short dresses, cloche hats, Eaton crop, Coco Chanel designs, shed fabric), Clara Bow's 1922 film Beyond the Rainbow, Zelda Fitzgerald as a real-life it girl, and the end of the era with the 1929 stock market crash and Depression.
topics: World War I impact on women

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the Short Stuff episode and set up the 1915 introduction of the word flapper.

segments.title: Mencken and the word flapper
segments.summary: H. L. Mencken's 1915 essay in The Smart Set popularized the term flapper, which had earlier been British slang for a young girl, to describe a new generation of young women breaking from tradition.

segments.title: Gibson Girl and the origins of change
segments.summary: The flapper replaced the Gibson Girl look created by illustrator Charles Dana Gibson. World War I and the 1918 flu pandemic changed gender norms and opened opportunities for women in work and education.
topics: World War I impact on women

segments.title: Suffrage, Prohibition and the new woman
segments.summary: Around 1920 the Roaring Twenties brought a new woman, shaped by the 18th Amendment (Prohibition, which fueled underground bars) and the 19th Amendment (women's right to vote). Flappers defied Victorian codes by smoking, drinking and wearing makeup.

segments.title: Automobiles and radio
segments.summary: The rise of the automobile let young women and men date away from home, and radio, with KDKA in Pittsburgh as an early commercial station and more than 600 stations by 1924, spread music and movies featuring the new style.

segments.title: Clara Bow, Zelda Fitzgerald and it girls
segments.summary: Clara Bow's 1922 film Beyond the Rainbow helped define the flapper look, and Zelda Fitzgerald was a real-life flapper and early it girl. Josh corrects himself that Clara Bow was the first it girl.

segments.title: Flapper fashion
segments.summary: Coco Chanel designs and the Victorian corset silhouette was replaced by boyish bodies and drapey, boxy sack dresses. Flapper dresses used far less fabric than Victorian gowns, hemlines rose from mid-calf to above the knee by the late 1920s, cloche hats and the Eaton crop were popular, arms were shown, and stockings were rolled down.

segments.title: End of the flapper era
segments.summary: The flapper era ended by 1929 with the Great Depression and the stock market crash of October 29, 1929, and Prohibition also ended.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode and note the show is a production of iHeartRadio.
